A cat(1) clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration.

## Key Features ### Syntax highlighting `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. ### Git integration `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. ### Show non-printable characters You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. ### Automatic paging By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. #### File concatenation Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. ## How to use Display a single file on the terminal: ```bash bat README.md ``` Display multiple files at once: ```bash bat src/*.rs ``` Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: ```bash curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat ``` Read from stdin, specify the language explicitly: ```bash yaml2json .travis.yml | json_pp | bat -l json ``` Show and highlight non-printable characters: ```bash bat -A /etc/hosts ``` Use it as a `cat` replacement: ```bash bat > note.md # quickly create a new file bat header.md content.md footer.md > document.md bat -n main.rs # show line numbers (only) bat f - g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. ``` ### Integration with other tools #### `fzf` You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: ```bash fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" ``` #### `find` or `fd` Preview all search results with `bat`: ```bash find … -exec bat {} + fd … -X bat ``` #### `ripgrep` With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: ```bash batgrep needle src/ ``` #### `tail -f` `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: ```bash tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log ``` #### `git` Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: ```bash git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs ``` #### `git diff` Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: ```bash batdiff() { git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff } ``` #### `xclip` Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: ```bash bat main.cpp | xclip ``` `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. #### `man` `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: ```bash export MANPAGER="bat -plman" man 2 select ``` #### Highlighting `--help` messages You can use `bat` to colorize help text: ```bash cp --help | bat -plhelp ``` Or use a wrapper: ```bash alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' help() { "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp } ``` ## Installation Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. `bat` is also available through various package managers: - Ubuntu/Debian: `sudo apt install bat` - Alpine: `apk add bat` - Arch: `pacman -S bat` - Fedora: `dnf install bat` - Gentoo: `emerge sys-apps/bat` - FreeBSD: `pkg install bat` - OpenBSD: `pkg_add bat` - Nix: `nix-env -i bat` - openSUSE: `zypper install bat` - macOS (Homebrew): `brew install bat` - macOS (MacPorts): `port install bat` - Windows (WinGet): `winget install sharkdp.bat` - Windows (Chocolatey): `choco install bat` - Windows (Scoop): `scoop install bat` ## Customization ### Highlighting theme Use `bat --list-themes` to get a list of all available themes for syntax highlighting. To select a theme, use the `--theme` option: ```bash bat --theme=TwoDark myfile.txt ``` Or set the `BAT_THEME` environment variable: ```bash export BAT_THEME="TwoDark" ``` `bat` automatically picks a fitting theme depending on your terminal's background color. You can use the `--theme-dark` / `--theme-light` options or the `BAT_THEME_DARK` / `BAT_THEME_LIGHT` environment variables to customize the themes used. ### Output style Use the `--style` option to control the appearance of `bat`'s output: ```bash bat --style=numbers,changes myfile.txt ``` Set the `BAT_STYLE` environment variable to make these changes permanent. ### Decorations By default, `bat` only shows decorations when outputting to an interactive terminal. Control this with the `--decorations` option: ```bash bat --decorations=always myfile.txt # always show decorations bat --decorations=never myfile.txt # never show decorations ``` ### Using a different pager `bat` uses the pager specified in the `PAGER` environment variable. If not set, `less` is used by default. You can also use bat's built-in pager with `--pager=builtin`. To use a different pager: ```bash export BAT_PAGER="less -RF" ``` ### Configuration file `bat` can be customized with a configuration file. To get the default path: ```bash bat --config-file ``` Generate a default configuration file: ```bash bat --generate-config-file ``` The configuration file is a simple list of command line arguments. Example: ```bash # Set the theme --theme="TwoDark" # Show line numbers, Git modifications and file header --style="numbers,changes,header" # Use C++ syntax for Arduino .ino files --map-syntax "*.ino:C++" ``` ## Command-line options For a full list of options, run: ```bash bat --help ``` ## Project goals `bat` tries to achieve the following goals: - Provide beautiful, advanced syntax highlighting - Integrate with Git to show file modifications - Be a drop-in replacement for (POSIX) `cat` - Offer a user-friendly command-line interface ## License Copyright (c) 2018-2025 bat-developers `bat` is made available under the terms of either the MIT License or the Apache License 2.0, at your option. {
	# Do not escape if completing a quoted value.
	[[ $cur == [\"\']* ]] && return 0
	if ((
		BASH_VERSINFO[0] > 5 || \

	elif ((
		BASH_VERSINFO[0] > 4 || \
		BASH_VERSINFO[0] == 4 && BASH_VERSINFO[1] > 0
	)); then
		# printf -v to an array index is available in bash >= 4.1.
		# Use it if available, as -o filenames is semantically
		# incorrect if we are not actually completing filenames, and it
		# has side effects (e.g. adds trailing slash to candidates
		# matching present dirs).
		local i
		for i in ${!COMPREPLY[*]}; do
			printf -v "COMPREPLY[i]" %q "${COMPREPLY[i]}"
